note: Seed map — bootstrapped from 20 MLOps scenario clusters. Cold-start track for learner with no prior ML/AI industry experience.

concepts.name: ML data pipeline anatomy
concepts.description: How raw data flows from source → ingestion → validation → feature store → training. Each stage's failure mode.

concepts.name: feature engineering and feature stores
concepts.description: Transforming raw signals into model inputs. Online vs offline feature stores, point-in-time correctness, feature reuse across models.

concepts.name: data drift and distribution shift
concepts.description: When production data diverges from training data. Covariate shift, label shift, concept drift — detection methods (PSI, KS test, JS divergence).

concepts.name: data versioning and reproducibility
concepts.description: Pinning dataset snapshots so any model can be re-trained exactly. DVC, Delta Lake, data contracts. The broken-schema failure mode.

concepts.name: training loop mechanics
concepts.description: Epochs, batches, learning rate schedules, gradient accumulation. What each training hyperparameter controls and its failure signature.

concepts.name: experiment tracking and reproducibility
concepts.description: MLflow, W&B, Neptune. What to log (params, metrics, artifacts, environment). Comparing runs. The unreproducible experiment failure mode.

concepts.name: overfitting, underfitting, and model selection
concepts.description: Bias-variance tradeoff in practice. Train/val/test discipline. Cross-validation. When to stop training. Hyperparameter search (grid, random, Bayesian).

concepts.name: offline evaluation and metric selection
concepts.description: Choosing the right metric for the business problem. AUC vs F1 vs precision@K. The metrics-business-outcome mismatch failure mode.

concepts.name: model packaging and serving contracts
concepts.description: Serialisation formats (ONNX, TorchScript, SavedModel). Input/output schema contracts. Why the training-serving skew problem exists.

concepts.name: inference serving infrastructure
concepts.description: Model servers (TorchServe, Triton, BentoML, vLLM for LLMs). REST vs gRPC. Batching strategies. GPU vs CPU serving tradeoffs.

concepts.name: deployment strategies
concepts.description: Blue/green, canary, shadow mode, A/B. When to use each. Rollback triggers. Champion-challenger pattern for model updates.

concepts.name: latency, throughput, and SLA management
concepts.description: p50/p95/p99 latency. Throughput vs latency tradeoff. Model quantisation, distillation, caching as levers. What breaks SLA and why.

concepts.name: production monitoring architecture
concepts.description: What to monitor: input distribution, prediction distribution, business KPI, system metrics. Log pipelines, dashboards, alert thresholds.

concepts.name: silent failures and debugging production models
concepts.description: Model serves without errors but predictions are wrong. Root-cause pattern: data pipeline change, feature skew, upstream schema change. Slice analysis.

concepts.name: retraining triggers and continuous training
concepts.description: Schedule-based vs performance-based vs data-trigger-based retraining. Automated pipelines. When NOT to retrain (instability, cost, data poisoning risk).

concepts.name: containerisation and reproducible environments
concepts.description: Docker for ML: pinning CUDA, Python, library versions. The works-on-my-machine failure mode. Multi-stage builds for lean serving images.

concepts.name: ML pipeline orchestration
concepts.description: Airflow, Kubeflow, Prefect, Metaflow. DAG structure: data → train → evaluate → register → deploy. Failure recovery, retries, parameterisation.

concepts.name: model registry and artifact management
concepts.description: MLflow Model Registry, SageMaker Model Registry. Versioning trained models, staging → production promotion gates, lineage tracking.

concepts.name: compute resource management and cost optimisation
concepts.description: Spot instances for training, reserved for serving. GPU utilisation, right-sizing. Auto-scaling inference. The cost spike failure mode.

concepts.name: end-to-end MLOps system design
concepts.description: Designing a full ML platform for a new use case: data → features → train → evaluate → serve → monitor → retrain loop. Tradeoffs at each layer.
